I used to play this game when it was only on the net and decided to try it again. It's quite the slow game which makes it perfect for a separate monitor. While I watch movies or TV shows it sits off to the side and does it's thing. It still requires planning and thought, so you can't just buy every upgrade you come across. I'm really enjoying the game and I'm looking forward to more content.

It's one of my two favorite Idle games, the other is Melvor Idle. Melvor has some action and is more interactive and has graphics. Kittens game however, it isn't flashy. But it's an unapologetic meme and it is really fun to explore. The religion and space parts of the game are really unexpected, and I have had a lot of fun over the year. Genuinely, I'm so excited to see this game come to Steam and get more updates. 

You can play it free on mobile or browser, but the desktop/Steam app does have some niceties. And also I really wanna support the dev after all the years I've enjoyed this game. If you like idle or incremental games, give it a go.

reviews.title: It’s pretty good but has a few issues
reviews.text:
Overall this is a good game. It gets to be a bit of a slog at certain points, and there’s zero explanation for what anything does or what to do, so you are just kinda flailing in the dark your first playthrough. Which is fine, but it can be really intimidating and I almost quit several times out of frustration at my lack of progress. I did enjoy it, but I’m going to be clear: the turn off pollution switch does nothing. It’s a straight up lie.
 I’m fine with the creator choosing not to have the ability to turn off pollution, but I’m not down with being lied to. It made me really suspicious about what other things in the game are lies or at least misrepresented, and I’ve definitely found a few.
The game messes up very small percentages so you get less than you were promised (looking at you, alicorns,) and there’s no correlation between real life time and time in the game. Something will sa

reviews.title: First Idle Game
reviews.text:
It’s okay I guess. I’ve never played an idle game before. At first, getting alerted when something was ready was fun and exciting. Now it just seems boring. That’s not the game’s fault though — and if you like idle clickers, this is clearly the queen. There’s a lot to unlock, it seems. The descriptions of each upgrade makes me smile too. Very clever. I don’t mind spending the $2.

But if you want something similar to A Dark Room, this isn’t it. If you want something with a fair bit of micromanaging, this isn’t it. If you want something where you’re actually doing something, this isn’t it. Some people say this has a little more to do than most idle games. It doesn’t have much to do, though. After about an hour you have to wait for stuff to automatically get researched and whatnot. You don’t get to do anything.

I still like it. It’s just not my favorite game. And I’ll still play something

reviews.title: Perfect Game, Bad Creator and Politics
reviews.text: I love idle games like this! I enjoyed the simple design that hides a great degree of choice and customization to optimize your society. It was shaping up to be one of my favorite mobile games. The part that warranted this one star in my mind was with the policy tab. In it you can use various societal policies to influence the growth of your cats. At first this was cool, until you unlocked more complex policies. The best policies number-wise were in reality monstrous. The fascist policy gives great optimization with almost no drawbacks, but the socialism policy costs a great deal of resources and literally does nothing(it even says it in the purchase description). This seems to be the creators attempt at a joke but it ignores the real world effects fascist governments have had. Also the only hostile species you interact with are the zebras which feels like a racist dig at Africa. I wante

reviews.title: A masterpiece of game design
reviews.text:
There are a lot of games nowadays that have gorgeous art and sprawling worlds and are extremely boring to play because the game itself is so poorly designed.

This is the antithesis of that. It’s got a janky interface, there are a bunch of themes that make it decent to look at but the UI is clearly an afterthought. It’s got some bugs and it’s mostly text based. There’s no astounding art here.

But the gameplay is so thoroughly well designed that it makes up for that tenfold. Calling it an idle game is almost a disservice, it definitely can be played as an idle game if you just want to wait and click but the mechanics are so interactive that you can spend hours in the app micromanaging what your kittens are doing and reducing wait times to mere minutes.

There are big difficulty spikes but they’re quickly followed by new mechanics to reach them, there are callbacks to your humble beginnin

reviews.title: Great game, but buggy
reviews.text: I’ve played this game years ago on PC and loved it, but once I got to concrete huts I stopped playing. I bought it on mobile thinking i’d replay and it’d be easier to come back often on my phone. It’s the same great game, and I love the portability, but the UI is mad buggy. The screen jumps when resources per second change, and logging into cloud saves made it so that every time I open the app it’s like a new game, I have to log in and load my save, and sometimes i’m missing production time or things i built. It blows to wait an hour to cap my resources and when I start the game it’s right where I left it like no time had passed, or it didn't save the building I spent a ton of stuff on. Other than the app being bad, 5/5 game

reviews.title: Great Game, Wonky UI
reviews.text:
one of the all time greats in terms of this genre, gets to the heart of what makes these games fun, big recommend.

HOWEVER, the interface gets a bit wonky and often times I’ll be pressing a button and hit another, and this keeps going and will only be fixed by restarting, which can be frustrating. it’s definitely possible my old phone is agitating the situation, but i also don’t have these problems with any other game or app, so i think i can safely say that it’s this game’s interface that doesn’t work quite properly. 

still, good stuff devs!

reviews.title: Makes Cookie Clicker Feel Like a One-Trick Pony
reviews.text:
I have been playing this game for the last couple of weeks in the background, and it's time for me to admit it—I am seriously hooked! This game has some serious depth to it. Like Cookie Clicker, but with actual strategy elements. And unlike most clicker games, you slowly unlock new game elements through multiple playthroughs.

The game never hits that point in most clicker offshoots where your progression goes from sluggish to laughably, exponentially fast. I think that aspect makes the progression feel more even, and gives the game staying power.

I much prefer the iPad app over the browser game, since I can take it on the go and have kind of a wimpy computer that gets sluggish when I keep it running constantly. The iPad app is attractive and has worked flawlessly for me.

If you read up on the game online, you'll quickly find people who have been playing regularly for several years. Th

reviews.title: Great incremental game!
reviews.text:
If you love a minimalist approach to what cookie clicker was, and add many resources, you get Kittens Game. One of the best, if not the best game of its kind I’ve played on the App Store.

I bought it off a whim and I don’t regret it. 1.99$ makes up for whatever ads or cash store that would have been implemented by a long shot. Most games have an ad every minute or less and light also have a store, while with this game you get a game. No in app purchases, no annoying ads. Just a plain and simple game that you can enjoy.

The only reason I can see this app not getting a 5 star review from all users would be because of the iPhone X support not being available yet the game is still purchase-able. So, if you have an X, make sure to see if the game has updated its compatibility for you.

I don’t want to spoil anything in this review, so take it from me. If you think you’d be interested in thi

reviews.title: Great game UI needs work
reviews.text: Overall I have played on mobile for years and desktop the same. 10/10 game but the sidebar scrolling has been broken for that same amount of time where you cannot scroll to the last resources in the list to craft. Thorium requires a lot of craft all maintenance on mobile and it’s crazy this hasn’t been fixed for as long as the bug has been in the game on mobile. Fix it and 5/5 granted

reviews.title: Unbelievably good
reviews.text:
I would give this game 6 stars if I could.  I’m blown away by the depth of this game.  It starts off simply enough but you just keep unlocking more and more things that keep the game fresh and intriguing.  It’s got a ton of depth and really is much more strategic than any other idle game I’ve ever played.  It puts every other idle game to shame, really.

I’ve been playing this for weeks now, and have only reset once just to see what bonus I might get.  The depth here is astounding and I will probably been playing it for weeks and months to come.

reviews.title: Amazing with a teeny problem.
reviews.text: I love this game! So much so that I got the app and I play on my school computer at school with free time and my laptop at home. It’s a great idler for a lot of fun development. Be wary, this game does take a while to develop. The gameplay is VERY SLOW, but it makes every accomplishment AWESOME! The only problem I have seen (thus far) is that, once you get more buildings, your “Refine Catnip” and “Harvest Catnip” button disappear. I can’t seem to put them back. To those who know, get the workshop asap so you can avoid this mistake. Otherwise, I love this game!

reviews.title: This is a perfect game!
reviews.text:
Everything about bringing this game to mobile is amazing. But it. Don’t even think about it. Can I send tips to you as well? I have two requests though!

1) Prevent screen jumping when numbers gain/lose digits. Switching to 3 decimal point precision works better, but it’s still a frustrating issue that has caused me to mistap things with grave consequences :/

2) This game would benefit so much from an optimized layout on the notched iPhones! I’m on the XS and would love love to see more info on the screen.

reviews.title: Fun Clicker Game
reviews.text:
Another fun clicker game much like Cookie Clicker (at first) but much less mindless. The progression is rewarding and keeps you hooked. Tiers are well structured and just when you think you have reached your limit and done all you can do, suddenly a bunch of new things are unlocked to mess around with and leave you questioning how you even struggled to create old resources while you begin the challenge of making new ones.

5 star gameplay, but needs some UI changes for smaller screens. Impossible to pull up the log on my iPhone Mini and the two-column layout feels quite cramped.

reviews.title: Lengthy and deep for an incremental game
reviews.text: You won’t be done with KG in a matter of days like some idle games. It has a great mix of logging on once in a while to tap a few progress bars and being able to sit down, plan, and finish research on something more in depth by actively playing the game. It’s less brainless than just tapping upgrades when they’re available and I really like that. I haven’t been this excited about an idle game since the Candy Box and Cookie Clicker days.

reviews.title: Great game! iPhone 11 support?
reviews.text: I’ve been playing this for 6 years now, and I have to say, LOVE the game. But, when I got the iPhone 11, the notch and the background of the screen was off. Borders were showing all over the place with white backgrounds (I have the inverted layout) and it is very hard to tap on the “observe” button when an astronomical event happens. Could you try to optimize the game more for iPhone 11?

reviews.title: Stimulating Adventure
reviews.text: Complex form and content synthesized with a simple skin of kittens creates a unique, mind boggling business and survival strategy adventure: Kittens Game. This app was worth twice the money as soon as I opened it. It’s fun, to say the least. It has me hooked, from waiting for my science to slowly creep high enough to buy the next social construct, or tapping furiously through a cold winter. I will definitely be looking forward to what this game has to offer in the future.

reviews.title: Fun idle game, but I have a few suggestions.
reviews.text: When I'm scrolling through the science menu quickly, it's hard to tell which options are completed and which options are available, could you give The option to hide them when they are completed? I have the same issue with the workshop too. If you implement these quality of life changes I'd be very happy.

reviews.title: Not for me
reviews.text: I loved A Dark Room and Universal Paperclips, so thought I would try this. Unfortunately, I am not having enough fun to continue. This game keeps unlocking more and more resources to keep track of, but all this complexity does not add enough depth as the rules are always the same: get resources, build everything. A story would make things better, but if there is one I haven’t found it after two hours. If you like heavy resource management games you might like this, but to me it feels more like a chore.

reviews.title: Game Breaking Bugs!!!!
reviews.text:
Save money and play on web browser!!!!

This is my favorite idle game ever but this mobile version has bugs that will prevent you from making any progress and breaking your game. For instance my current game doesn’t let me gather resources unless the game is on screen. As soon as I lock my phone or switch to another app all my kittens get unassigned from their jobs. Pretty frustrating when you can’t play an idle game the way it’s intended.

reviews.title: Virtual kitten civilization simulator in my phone
reviews.text: This game is too addictive comrade. Everyone works at the edge of the productivity curve depending on their happiness and access to rare resources . Go to space and get more resources. Hunt and sacrifice unicorns to get more happiness and resources . Bigger numbers and more things to track. No pictures necessary. Da, in post soviet Purrsia, work does YOU!  Download to this a game toest of the days and you will be enjoying this mit vodka como yo.

reviews.title: My favorite Incremental Game
reviews.text: I recently got back into Kitten’s Game and remembered why this is my favorite incremental game. Everything feels so unique, like this is its own little world that you are unraveling. You have to fight for progress but it feels great when you figure things out and move forward. Very much recommended.

reviews.title: Great Game, but mobile version should be updated.
reviews.text: I think that the mobile kittens game could be just as good as the browser version if there was an option to bulk craft resources instead of just spamming “refine capnip” for example. I hope this is taken into consideration by the developers.

reviews.title: Great adaption but I'm discouraged to play mobile.
reviews.text: I want to play this game on mobile, but background refresh makes it inconvenient for resources like spices, fur, and ivory unless I check back frequently early game. I'm also afraid of coming back to a graveyard if I go long enough without playing.

reviews.title: Best incremental game, few bugs
reviews.text: Best incremental game out there and on mobile. There are a few bugs compared to the browser version, for example: the science Ecology doesn't actually unlock solar farms so future workshop upgrades are rendered useless. Otherwise, 5 stars if all fixed.

reviews.title: Only game you need. For life.
reviews.text:
It feels like a journey.

The game has a very slow burn that takes multiple years to reach its full potential.

Read the wiki and understand the incredible depth of this one of a kind incremental text clicker.

There is awesome support from the community of players as well.  Some of them have been playing for several years.

I have been playing for over 2 years myself and my journey is far from over.

The only game I might play till I die.

-hellwitch

reviews.title: It’s been a while so I’m starting my fourth replay from scratch!
reviews.text: I adore this game, thank you for keeping it active. This is my first run since pollution was added and it adds a really nice friction to the early game

reviews.title: Fantastic game, one bug
reviews.text: It’s a really good game and I was checking in every night to buy barns and strategise saving when at year 459 I stopped be able to make idle progress and as soon as I left the game the time reset to year 459. I reset time to no avail.

reviews.title: Great game!
reviews.text: KG is a well-balanced and shockingly deep resource management semi-idle game. So well-crafted in the way it introduces and repeats various tactics and game concepts while still managing to surprise, with a clever slow-reveal narrative. Easily worth $0.99, especially with no in-app purchases or ‘pay-to-play’ element. All of the stars for Kittens Game!

reviews.title: Fantastic but buggy game
reviews.text: This is an innovative and compelling game that unfolds as you play it. It’s really hard to put down and definitely worth checking out. That being said, the app has some pretty serious bugs and annoyances that make it just ok. I think playing the browser version is definitely the way to go.

reviews.title: Best long term clicker game
reviews.text: If you’re looking for an idle game that respects your time this is it. No graphics, no micro transactions, no bs. Pure clicker bliss. Had this game for years and it’s still fun. If you’re looking for something like this but that will las one day check out universal Paperclips

reviews.title: Great! But please add a hold button mechanism...
reviews.text: I’ve recently discovered this game and I’ve enjoyed it. The only complaint is the amount of clicking has been tiresome on a small phone. Just a hold option would be a mercy for my poor muscles.

reviews.title: Awesome Idle Game
reviews.text: I’ve been playing the browser version for years. The app is great because now I take my current game anywhere. I don’t have to run several different games on different computers.

reviews.title: Simple and amazing!
reviews.text: This game is so simple, yet so deep and fun. The balance is perfect at keeping you interested and always looking forward to the next upgrade. This is the best incremental game i have played. Worth every penny and more!

reviews.title: Great incremental idle game
reviews.text: This game has depth and continues to change with each reset. Even with minimal graphics I’ve played this idle game longer than any other at this point. Be warned, this game is gruelingly long though.

reviews.title: Love it, but I think I found a bug
reviews.text: Solar farms didn’t unlock. I don’t think this is because I did anything wrong. Despite this, I love this game and am fascinated by my kittens (who are happy fascists) descending deeper and deeper into religious zealotry.

reviews.title: Glitch found
reviews.text:
Amphitheaters are not reducing unhappiness.  The population I have is 10 kittens and 90% happiness so I built two amphitheatres to reduce the unhappiness but the happiness is still at 90%.

I played this on Kongregate and liked it so much I decided to get it for my iPad.  Hope this gets fixed so I can continue the game without mad kittens.

reviews.title: Late game issues
reviews.text:
Late game has a lot of issues, both game balance wise as well as calculations. 
Also it doesn’t support resuming from multitasking so if you have a lot of apps open be prepared to restart often.

reviews.title: Clocked in 100s of hours
reviews.text: This game is a punishing strategy game which punishes your incorrect decisions by wasting your most valuable resource: time. This high stakes decision forces you to play the game with an attention to detail, and forces investment in an amazing way.

reviews.title: Game is super fun but app needs polish
reviews.text: I'm loving this game, but please for the love of god fix the UI issue where text stutters back and forth over newline wrapping boundaries as decimals change

reviews.title: Buggy
reviews.text: I truly enjoy this game, but I spent $2 on it and wish that it wouldn’t be so buggy. Biggest complaint is closing the app makes in game progress reset constantly. The game is slow enough already without having to redo things 2 or 4 times.

reviews.title: This game needs more spotlight!
reviews.text: This game deserves more attention. Especially in a world of micro transactions. I love the slow but rewarding milestones you hit with your cats! It’s worth every penny of the one time fee.

reviews.title: Pls don’t stop developing
reviews.text: Wish this game got more love I love idle games and this is one of the best. Pls don’t stop updating this game I love it simple but complex I would spend 10 bucks just to get a version 2

reviews.title: Pollution
reviews.text: This game would be 5 stars if pollution was removed as a feature. It’s so unbelievably unfun and their attempt at a joke with the ‘disable pollution’ option - that does nothing - is just a slap in the face as well. Why ruin your own game and not offer the people who support you an option that would keep people playing. Boo 👎🏻

reviews.title: Good mechanics horrible ui
reviews.text: Coming from the browser version the ui of the mobile version needs a rework. All the text is super small and it is overall super cluttered. I would just play it on the website instead.

reviews.title: Broken UI for iPhone XS Max
reviews.text: The UI for the game is broken for iPhone XS Max, the event window on the bottom of the screen hides if you scroll up from the bonfire menu or any menu, also if you go into the event window the close button hides if you scroll up to view the most recent events. Gameplay is 10/10 been playing daily for over a month.

reviews.title: Purrrfect transition
reviews.text: I loved the original version of the game and I'm happy to purchase a mobile version I can take anywhere.

reviews.title: Great on PC, UI needs work
reviews.text: Love playing the game on computer browser but the mobile UI is pretty awful and it looses some of the games functionality like the ability the pawse the game. If I had known before I bought the app I wouldn’t have.

reviews.title: Poor progression
reviews.text: This game really stalls out. I played for 3 weeks and it had almost no progression. Additionally, the game does not save every time you exit the app so you can repeat the same block, over and over without realizing it.

reviews.title: Progress Wipes
reviews.text: Decided to pick this up again and my progress constantly keeps wiping. It’s great to have cloud saves but when that doesn’t automatically get saved you’re going back to the last time you manually did it.

reviews.title: It’s a good game!
reviews.text:
When I quit the game and re-entry,app will show me the black screen for a long time. Please solve this problem,thanks.
退出游戏重新进入会黑屏一段时间，不知道是bug还是啥，希望作者能看到。

reviews.title: Doesn’t autosave
reviews.text: The game randomly autosaves, which is incredibly irritating as Ill come back to the game to find 10 or 20 minutes of progress gone

reviews.title: Game is fun but the layout is....not great
reviews.text:
This is a very well done and in depth game. However the UI is terribly done and doesn't actually property fit the phone :/

reviews.title: Best clicker I've ever played
reviews.text:
Played these games addictively since the old cookie clicker days (the real one, not one of the thousands of knockoffs!). Compared to the rest of the genre, it's like what "spore" tried to be, but it actually works. You don't just buy buildings that go from "hut" to "space station" or whatever, you actually evolve the gameplay again and again, so that new and interesting mechanics keep arising even after months of play.

Just, y'know, play responsibly ;)
